title: A disputed election intensifies the legitimacy crisis
detail: The February 1996 parliamentary election, boycotted by major opposition parties, deepened doubts about whether elections under an incumbent partisan framework could command public legitimacy.

title: Parliament passes the Thirteenth Amendment
detail: The Constitution (Thirteenth Amendment) Act created a non-party caretaker government system to supervise parliamentary elections and reduce partisan mistrust at the point of transfer of power.

title: The caretaker framework is tested in a national election
detail: The first election under the new framework became a practical test of whether constitutional neutrality could restore broader participation and confidence in the electoral process.

title: The framework becomes the center of later constitutional conflict
detail: What began in 1996 as a compromise later became the central reference point for the 2006-2008 crisis, judicial review, and the 2011 abolition of the caretaker system.
